speaker: Doctor
text:
Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a chronic wound on your right lower leg; can you tell me how long it has been there and if it was present before you started wearing your current shoes?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
REQUEST TEST: Blood Glucose HbA1c

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: WBC: Within normal limits, Hemoglobin: Within normal limits, Platelets: Within normal limits; Blood Glucose HbA1c: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
Good news, those blood tests indicate your immune system is functioning normally and there is no evidence of diabetes. Now, does the wound have a foul odor or appear to be discolored with black or brown tissue?

REQUEST TEST: Wound Culture
REQUEST TEST: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Wound Culture: No growth of pathogenic bacteria; Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR): NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
The wound culture and ESR are normal, suggesting this is likely not an active infection or a systemic inflammatory process like vasculitis. To better understand the underlying cause, are you experiencing any numbness, tingling, or a feeling of "pins and needles" in that leg, and do you have a history of smoking or peripheral artery disease?

REQUEST TEST: Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI)
REQUEST IMAGES: Lower_Leg_Wound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI): NORMAL READINGS; Lower_Leg_Wound: Large ulcer on the right lower leg, presence of varicose veins, edema in both legs (more pronounced in the right), diminished dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses on the right, skin discoloration with chronic changes, evidence of venous reflux and obstruction in superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ABI is normal, ruling out significant arterial blockage, and your wound image clearly shows varicose veins, edema, and venous reflux. Given these findings, do you recall if the wound improves significantly when you elevate your leg above heart level?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That family history of leg problems and your prior deep vein thrombosis strongly suggest a venous etiology. Does your right leg feel noticeably heavier or more swollen than the left when standing for a long time?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Venous Insufficiency with Venous Stasis Ulcer
